rows.title_full: AN ACT DEREGULATING CERTAIN PUBLIC SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 146, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Franchises to render specific public services may be extended to one or a limited number of private enterprises in a specified service area, if necessary to encourage private enterprises to render such public service. The best qualified and most capable to render such public service shall be elected in the required number from among competing applicants. Such franchises have the effect of limiting normal competition in rendering the public service, and are therefore subject to regulation by thedesignated agency of government.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MAINTAINING THE PRESENT PROVISION ON PROBATIONARY EMPLOYMENT INCREASING AT THE SAME TIME THE GOVERNMENT'S PROTECTION TO PROBATIONARY EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 281 OF THE LABOR CODE
rows.abstract: Probationary employment shall not exceed six months from the date the employees started working, unless it is covered by an apprenticeship agreement stipulating a longer period. The services of an employee who has been engaged on a probationary basis may  be terminated for a just cause or when he fails to qualify as a regular employee in accordance with reasonable standards made known by the employer to the employee at the time of his engagement. An employee who is allowed to work after a probationary period whether broken or not shall be considered a regular employee.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING BREASTFEEDING BY ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING LACTATION STATIONS IN WORKPLACES FOR WORKING MOTHERS, PROVIDING FOR ITS VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Breastfeeding Promotion Act".  It is hereby mandated that lactations shall be established in workplaces for nursing female employees, which must have a lavatory for hand-washing, refrigeration for storing and comfortable seats. > Subject to such regulations as the Secretary of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) may presribe, nursing female employees  are given reasonable time during working hours to express their milk in the lactation station in their workplace, which time shall beconsidered as compensable hours worked.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06661

rows.author: C062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST HABITUAL WIFE BEATING, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to promote and protect the welfare of women, and preserve their dignity as human person. towards this end, the government shall protect women against habitual wife beating from their spouse. Habitual wife beating shallbe prohibited whether or not there is provocation on the aprt of the victim. For the purpose of this Act, habitual wife beating shall mean the infliction of physical injuries by the husband upon his wife for at tleast (2) times within a period of one(1) year, regardless of whether or not the spouse are living together.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05516

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTE POLICIES TO ELIMINATE THE TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS ESPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS, ESTABLISHING THE NECESSARY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION AND SUPPORT OF TRAFFICKED PERSONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Trafficking in persons shall refer to the recruitment, transfer or deployment of a person with or without the victim's consent or knowledge, through legal or illegal means, fraud or deceit, violence, coercion, intimidation, abuse of position or authority, within or across national borders for purposes of prostitution, or work or services, marriage or adoption and other similar arrangements, characterized by forced labor and slavery-like practices, sexual exploitation and other similar acts.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04432

rows.title_full: AN ACT INTEGRATING GENDER AND DEVELOPMENT ISSUES AND CONCERNS IN ALL CURRICULA OF ALL LEVELS OF EDUCATION AND TRAINING IN ALL SCHOOLS AND UNIVERSITIES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The integration of Geneder and Development (GAD) issues and concerns in the curricula of all levels of education and trainings in all schools and universities of the country is important to our own citizenship, and to our own local governance, as itwill seeks to highlight the key concepts of geneder and development - sustainable development, social justice and equality, family relations and population, sound values and perceptions, roles of women and men, diversity, conflict resolutions, humanrights and among others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF THE PHILIPPINES, STRENGTHENING ITS POWERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish the National Archives, granting it powers and appropriations for its opertions. The Office shall be under the Department of Education, Culture and Sports and shall take over the Records and Management Archives Office created in 1958. It shall plan, develop, prescribe, disseminate and enforce policies, rules and regulations and coordinate government wide programs governing the general protection, use, maintenance, storage and disposition of public records.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE WATER POLLUTION CONTROL POLICY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Philippine Clean Water Act of 2001". This bill seeks to provide for a comprehensive water pollution control policy. It shall cover all water resources such as inland surface waters, ground waters, wetlands, coastal and marine waters within the Philippine territory and area of responsibility. It shall also cover all potential sources of water pollution.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05398

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENTS (IRA) OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, (LGUS) IN PROVIDING FOR ITS EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION, AUTHORIZING ITS AUTOMATIC RETENTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 284, 285 AND 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill calls for the amendment of the Local Government Code by increasing the allotment in the internal revenue taxes of local government units. From the present forty, it will be increased to sixty percent at a rate of five percent per annum over a period of four year effective the immediately proceeding fiscal year.> The bill likewise seeks equitable distribution of the IRA after the deduction of the costs of devolution. Finally, it mandates the automatic retention of the IRA such that theLGU will have immediate access to all the funds it needs for its operations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CREDIT ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR OVERSEAS WORKERS
rows.abstract: An overseas contract worker with a valid contract through/from an accredited employment of the POEA may avail of a loan of not more than Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) from the Overseas Worker Welfare Administration (OWWA) to defray the living expenses of his family during the first months of absence as well as recruitment expenses including placement fees, documentation costs and plant tickets. Mode of payment and sanctions are, likewise, provided.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT COMMITTED BY ANY PERSON WITHOUT LICENSE OR AUTHORITY, AMENDING TITLE II, ARTICLE 7 OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OVERSEAS MIGRANT WORKERS' ACT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: As we continue to suffer from the lack of employment opportunities in our shores and as we continue to promote overseas employment for our people, we likewise need to continue to strengthen our laws on illegal recruitment. This bill mandates the increase of penalty of illegal recruitment without license or authority, amending the Overseas Migrant Worker's Law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY, STABILIZE PRICES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS AND ENHANCE FOOD SECURITY THROUGH THE EFFECTIVE PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, MARKETING AND DISTRIBUTION OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, RATIONALIZING AND RESTRUCTURING FOR THE PURPOSE, ALL EXISTING GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, DISTRIBUTION, MARKETING AND OTHER SUPPORT PROGRAMS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Agricultural Markeing Act of 2001". This bill aims to achieve the best administration of market development programs for agricultural commodities and food products and ensure a fair return to producers as well as an adequate flow of agricultural products to consumers. It seeks to prevent inefficient and wasteful methods of distribution and to assist in preventing shortages and managing surpluses of agricultural commodities, so as to maintain efficient domestic markets and prevent imbalances from causing undue, excessive and destabilizing fluctuations in the prices of agricultural commodities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PHILIPPINE BUSINESS REGISTRY DATABANK
rows.abstract: The Databank shall be the main repository of pertinent information on business enterprises in the Philippines. It shall provide business information and training services in support of business development, capabilities and skills training. The focus of its assistance shall be the medium, small and micro enterprises.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING MANDATORY DRUG TESTING OF EMPLOYEES IN, AND APPLICANTS TO GOVERNMENT AGENCIES INVOLVED IN THE ADMINISTRATION OR ENFORCEMENT OF LAWS AGAIST DANGEROUS DRUGS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All employees in, and applicants for employment to government agencies principally and primarily charged with the administration or enforcement of laws against dangerous drugs such as but not limited to employees of the Dangerous Drugs Board, employees and guards of drug rehabilitation centers and agents and operatives of special police and military anti-drug units are hereby required to undergo a medical test to determine probable use of dangerous drugs.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THREE SMALL FARMERS' REPRESENTATIVES IN THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION (NIA) BOARD BY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-SIX HUNDRED AND ONE, AS AMENDED, `AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION' , ANDFOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The primary focus before of the NIA is to irrigate lands producing the most basic agricultural commodity, rice and corn. This is the primary reason why rice and corn farmers were given a right of representation in its Board of Director. As our farmers production has evolved into a variety of commodities, it is high time that representation in the NIA Board should be granted to those whose livelihood are very much dependent on it. These are small farmers who lacked the resources to irrigate thesmall landholding on their own.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL OFFICIAL NON WORKING DAYS TO FALL EITHER ON A MONDAY OR A FRIDAY
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to declare all official non-working days to fall either on a Monday or a Friday. It aims to prevent the happening of having "sandwiched" days. This will have a pleasant effect not merely to the business environment but likewise to the fields of education, government and social services.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REDUCTION OF THE FIVE (5)-YEAR QUALIFICATION PERIOD FOR THE PROSECUTION STAFF EXCLUDING THE CHIEF STATE PROSECUTOR AND THE THREE (3) ASSISTANTS CHIEF STATE PROSECUTORS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 3 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1275
rows.abstract: The Chief State Prosecutor, the three Assistants Chief State Prosecutors, [and the members of the Prosecution Staff] shall be selected from among qualified and professionally trained members of the legal profession who are of proven integrity and competence and have been in the actual practice of the legal profession for at least five (5) years prior to their appointment or have held during like period, any position requiring the qualifications of a lawyer. rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING GRADUATES OF CRIMINOLOGY FROM ANY ACCREDITED PHILIPPINE SCHOOL OF CRIMINOLOGY TO BE ENLISTED AND APPOINTED AS MEMBERS OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE WITHOUT NEED OF TAKING THE QUALIFYING ENTRANCE EXAMINATION AS REQUIRED FOR BY SECTION 32 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1990
rows.abstract: Rationale: Records have it that the country today is in dire need of the services of additional policemen not only because of the prevailing crime rate but also because we are way below the standard on "police and population ratio".> Year in and year out, our accredited criminology schools turn out hundreds of graduates who have undergone four year of training in criminology thereby making them a rich source of future policemen. Presently, however, this source has not been fully utilized.

rows.abstract: Any provision of  existing laws, rules and regulations to the contrary notwithstanding , it shall be unlawful for any eductional institution offering courses requiring board, bar or any licensing examination from compelling their respective graduates to take review classes and or pre-board examinations in the school or college of which the student is a graduate. rows.abstract: Rationale: The shortfall in housing  stems from one major problem: government and its inability to put its act together. The sheer number of agencies tasked with addressing the problem has indiscriminatel y resulted in the duplication of functions and made for a policy environment that is described, at best, as incoherent. Towards this end, it proposes the creation of the Department of Housing and Urban Development.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to mandate local government units to set aside not less than two and a half percent (2.5%) of the total revenue from regular sources of the preceding year for reforestation programs and projects. Setting aside two and a half percent(2.5%) of the LGUs total revenue from regular sources of the preceding year, ensures the LGUs ecological viability and enhances the country's resources sustainability.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Senior citizens have lost  the vigor to engage in business or any gainful occupation due to their age. They only venture themselves in banking business by way of depositing their money which they received after retirement from service (retirement benefits), hoping to earn from the privilege interest rate provided by the banking institutions, in which the interest income is the only appropriate income for them to sustain daily life. rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR THE REDUCTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOCATION (IRAs) OF HIGH-INCOME LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) BY EIGHT PERCENT (8%) FORTHE BENEFIT OF LOW INCOME LGUs
rows.abstract: Rationale: The provision of Section 285 of RA 7160 is hereby amended to rectify the unfair and inequitable allocation of IRA of LGUs. To make the present system more responsive to the needs of low-income LGUs, this bill proposes to reduce the IRAs of high-income LGUs for the benefit of low-income LGUs. The reduced IRA will be allocated in proportation to population density, poverty incidence, and income class of LGUs, in lieu of land area and equal sharing. The proposed method would enable thelow-income local government units to carry out devolved functions, particularly, health and agricultural services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.abstract: "Courses Accreditation Act of 2001". The State shall regulate the rights of students against academic institutions that exploit their innocence, powerlessness and timidity. rows.abstract: One of the proposed amendments to RA No. 7941, the Party-list System Act, is: "PROVIDED, THAT A POLITICAL PARTY SHALL NOT BE REGISTERED UNLESS IT IS ABLE TO SHOW PROOF THAT ITS CONTITUENCY IS SPREAD OVER THE GEOGRAPHICAL TERRITORY OF AT LEAST A MAJORITY OF THE REGIONS, OR AT LEAST A MAJORITY OF THE PROVINCES OR CITIES COMPRISING A REGION, AS MAYBE APPROPRIATE IN EACH CASE; AND PROVIDED FURTHER, THAT A SECTORAL PARTY, ORGANIZATION OR ANY COALITION THEREOF SHALL NOT BE REGISTERED UNLESS IT IS ABLE TO SHOW PROOF THAT IT REPRESENTS THE INTEREST AND CONCERNS OF AT LEAST THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND FILIPINO CITIZENS BELONGING TO OR SITUATED IN THAT SECTOR IT SEEKS TO REPRESENT."

rows.abstract: This bill seeks the creation of the Philippine Commission on women which will absorb the functions of the National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women (NCRFW), monitor the implementation of the laws on women, review and evaluate the extent to which women are integrated in all sectors of economic and social life.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE MEMBERS OF THE LUPONG TAGAPAMAYAPA MONTHLY HONORARIUM IN THE AMOUNT OF ONE THOUSAND PESOS (P1,000.00), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 406 OF THE `LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The system of amicably settling disputes (PD No. 1508) at the barangay level has promoted the speedy administration of justice and has strengthened the family as a basic institution. The success of the implementation of the Decree could not have been possible without the dedication of the hardworking members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa who sacrificed their time and efforts so that peace and order would reign in the barangay. These barangay officials deserve recognition and support.

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001 REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: At present, drug abuse has reached alarming proportions not only in the Philippines, but also in most regions of the world. With the proliferation of senseless crimes due to drug use and/or abuse, it is proposed that the minimum quantityprescribed in R.A. 6425, as amended be removed. Furthermore, in order to give more emphases on the responsibility of the parents to educate and discipline their minor children regarding the evils of using or consuming dangerous drugs, the parents under the proposed bill shall be civilly liable if their children are found guilty of violating the provisions of the Dangerous Drugs Act, as amended.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433
